## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 However, machine-assisted analysis through DharmaNexus demonstrates vast formulaic text-reuse within the Pali canon, recording 15,315 matching segments across 138 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its primary reuse partners are other chapters of the *Patthana* that deploy identical analytical templates, most prominently the *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13, sharing 306,831 characters), *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 1.3), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1), *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2), and *Vitakkattika* (Patthana 1.7) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-tradition DharmaNexus alignments identify shared doctrinal formulations with Sanskrit and Tibetan Abhidharma and scholastic works—such as Vīryaśrīdatta's *Arthaviniścayasūtra-nibandhana*, the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054), the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897), the *Yogācārabhūmi* (including the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, D4036), and the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā Lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093)—though these represent shared technical terminology and topical matrices rather than direct genetic parallels [DharmaNexus].
